analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/provider/sandboxes.md adds an "Use an external drive" section, and docs/provider/cli-reference.md documents the `darkbloom sandbox setup --disk <volume>` flag. No executable code changed. I examined sandboxes.md in full (patch hunks plus base text) and the visible head portions of cli-reference.md (lines 2487-3074). The `--disk` flag text in cli-reference.md (around base 1256-1300) was visible only as a truncated patch excerpt, so it was not fully reviewed.

The documented behavior touches TB-013/T-061 (sandbox installer and add-on run as the Mac owner) and A-019. The new `--disk` option passes absolute, user-chosen paths to the installer. The docs say setup checks each path with statfs, requires APFS, and does not format drives. The privileged action is `sudo diskutil enableOwnership <volume>`. It is run only after the user answers a prompt, and with `--yes` or no terminal it is printed rather than run. This is user-initiated, so no new authority is granted without consent.

The external-volume trust concerns match T-041's existing cache-storage text: peripheral controllers are untrusted, and UUID cloning, retained data and DoS are possible. Sandbox VM images and jobs on an external drive are a separate data path from the inference prefix cache. The docs do not claim confidentiality for them, and they state that jobs on a vanished drive are stopped and unpaid.

Unverified by the supplied evidence: the source implementing the `--disk` path validation (symlinks, path canonicalization, `~` handling, passing paths to install.sh as arguments with no shell injection) and the add-on 1.2.0 behavior. These are in SandboxAddon.swift and the add-on, neither supplied. A later pass should check them if the code ships in the same PR. The threat model may later need a note that sandbox work disks on external volumes are outside the attested boundary. I raise no finding here because the changes are documentation only.
